learningObjective: Explain what a SymInt is in PyTorch 2 and how it participates in the traced graph.

canonicalClaims.claim: A SymInt is a compile-time symbolic integer used by PyTorch 2's tracer (Dynamo/AOTAutograd) to represent dim values or arithmetic on them when the value is unknown at trace time; the graph is parameterized in these symbols and they are resolved to concrete integers at runtime.
conditions: Symbolic-shape tracing is enabled (mark_dynamic, dynamic=True, or automatic promotion).
nonImplications: Does not imply every op supports symbolic shapes cleanly; some fail to trace and fall back.
Does not imply a symbolic-shape kernel matches a specialized kernel in performance.

misconceptions.claim: A SymInt is a GPU tensor holding an integer value.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SymInts live in the tracing/compilation stack, not as device tensors.

misconceptions.claim: A SymInt is the average of previously seen dim values.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SymInts are symbolic; they do not encode statistical estimates.

misconceptions.claim: SymInt forces Triton kernels to be integer-only.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SymInts are unrelated to floating-point support in generated kernels.
Other guards (stride, dtype, unmarked dims) can still trigger recompiles.

implementationFacts: Symbols named `s0`, `s1`, ... in the traced graph
Arithmetic on SymInts is captured symbolically (e.g., `s0 * 4`)
performanceScenarios: SymInt-parameterized graphs reduce recompilation cost; extreme constraints or complex control flow may still specialize.
